summary.text: Alec Ferguson is the Victorian Socialists candidate for Bayswater at the 2026 Victorian election. He is a student of Arabic at Deakin University, where he helped organise pro-Palestinian student protests, including the 2024 encampment. He says he has been an activist since 2021, also campaigning on refugee rights, racism and climate change.

summary.text: David Kitchen is the Liberal candidate for Bayswater, a Labor-held seat whose MP is retiring at the 2026 Victorian election. A public servant, he is a former RAAF officer and began his working life at Victoria Police. His campaign material centres on crime, the cost of living and traffic on local roads.

summary.text: Gary Coombes is standing for Family First in Bayswater at the 2026 Victorian election. The ABC describes him as a retired electronics technician who has also run a business. He has contested Bayswater for Family First twice before, in 2010 and 2022, and stood for the party in the federal seats of Casey in 2013 and Deakin in 2016.

summary.text: Jess Kennedy is the Greens candidate for Bayswater at the 2026 Victorian election. She works in mental health as a worker and consultant, grew up in Melbourne's eastern suburbs, and spent eight years as a finance manager for a telecommunications company in the United Kingdom. She started a petition, sponsored in Parliament by Greens MLC Sarah Mansfield, calling for GPs to be able to diagnose and treat ADHD.

summary.text: Julie Buxton is standing for Labor in Bayswater at the 2026 Victorian election; the seat's Labor MP, Jackson Taylor, is retiring. She runs a bookkeeping and business services firm in Bayswater, and earlier worked in the public service and managed Taylor's electorate office. Labor ran her in Ferntree Gully at the 2018 state election, which she lost to Liberal Nick Wakeling.

summary.text: Mathew Clarke is an independent candidate for Bayswater at the 2026 Victorian election. He works in security and founded Melbourne Writers, a group that brings writers together, and his website says he spent ten years in the public service. He had planned to stand in the Melbourne district but, by his own account, could not collect enough nominating signatures in time and switched to Bayswater, where he grew up. He proposes that voters rate policy ideas submitted without the author's name, with the results guiding how he would vote.
